svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The neuromuscular junction: where a motor neurone meets a muscle fibre."], [1, "An action potential arrives at the axon terminal."], [2.5, "Voltage-gated calcium channels open; Ca\u00b2\u207a ions diffuse in."], [4.5, "Vesicles fuse with the membrane and release acetylcholine into the cleft (exocytosis)."], [7, "ACh diffuses across and binds receptors on the motor end plate; Na\u207a channels open and Na\u207a enters."], [10, "The muscle membrane depolarises: an action potential spreads along the fibre and it contracts."], [13, "Acetylcholinesterase breaks ACh down; choline returns to the neurone to be recycled."]]
svg.title: The neuromuscular junction
svg.desc: A motor neurone terminal with acetylcholine vesicles above a folded motor end plate: calcium enters, vesicles release acetylcholine, it binds receptors, sodium enters and the muscle fibre depolarises; acetylcholinesterase breaks acetylcholine down.
svg.text: Greatly magnified; the synaptic cleft is about 50 nm wide.

g.data-info: The end of a motor neurone axon, full of vesicles containing acetylcholine (ACh) and many mitochondria (ATP for making and releasing ACh).
Released by exocytosis into the synaptic cleft.
The action potential opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels; Ca²⁺ diffuses in and makes vesicles move to and fuse with the presynaptic membrane.
A gap of about 50 nm; ACh diffuses across it.
The action potential spreads along the sarcolemma and down the T-tubules, causing Ca²⁺ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and contraction.
g.text: muscle fibre (sarcolemma folded into the motor end plate)

g.data-name: ACh receptors on the motor end plate
g.data-info: Ligand-gated Na⁺ channels in the folded sarcolemma. ACh binding opens them: Na⁺ enters and depolarises the muscle fibre membrane.
g.aria-label: ACh receptors on the motor end plate

g.text: action potential along the muscle fibre → contraction

g.data-info: Enzyme in the cleft that hydrolyses ACh to choline and ethanoate (acetate), stopping continuous stimulation. Choline is taken back into the neurone to make more ACh.

g.text: ACh → choline + ethanoate; choline taken back up
